spots.name: White City
spots.summary: The White City is a collection of over 4,000 buildings in Tel Aviv from the 1930s built in a unique form of the International Style, commonly known as Bauhaus, by German Jewish architects who fled to the British Mandate of Palestine from Germany after the rise to power of the Nazis.

names.ja: テルアビブの白い都市

spots.name: Rothschild Boulevard
spots.summary: Rothschild Boulevard is one of the principal streets in the center of Tel Aviv, Israel, beginning in Neve Tzedek at its southeastern edge and running north to Habima Theatre. It is one of the most expensive streets in the city, being among one of its main tourist attractions.

spots.name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art

hours.note: Closed Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Tel Aviv Museum of Art is an art museum in Tel Aviv, Israel. The museum is dedicated to the preservation and display of modern and contemporary art both from Israel and around the world.

names.es: Museo de Arte de Tel Aviv

spots.name: Azrieli Center
spots.summary: Azrieli Center is a complex of three skyscrapers in Tel Aviv. At the base of the complex lies a large shopping mall. The complex was designed by Israeli-American architect Eli Attia.

spots.name: Jaffa Clock Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Jaffa Clock Tower stands in the middle of the north end of Yefet Street in Jaffa, Tel Aviv.

spots.name: Sarona
spots.summary: Sarona is a neighborhood of Tel Aviv, Israel which started as a German Templer colony in Ottoman Palestine in 1871. It was one of the earliest modern villages established by Europeans in Ottoman Palestine.

spots.name: Trumpeldor Cemetery
spots.summary: Trumpeldor Cemetery, often referred to as the "Old Cemetery," is a historic cemetery on Trumpeldor Street in Tel Aviv, Israel. The cemetery covers 10.6 dunams, and contains approximately 5,000 graves.

spots.name: Dizengoff Square
spots.summary: Dizengoff Square or Dizengoff Circus is a public square in Tel Aviv, on the corner of Dizengoff Street, Reines Street, and Pinsker Street. One of the city's main squares, it was built in 1934 and inaugurated in 1938.

spots.name: Hostages Square
spots.summary: Hostages Square is a public plaza located in front of the Tel Aviv Museum of Art. In the wake of the October 7 attacks, families of the hostages established a permanent encampment in the square due to its proximity to the Israel Defense Forces headquarters.

spots.summary: Shalom Meir Tower is an office tower in Tel Aviv, Israel.

spots.name: Tel Aviv Port
spots.summary: The Tel Aviv Port is a commercial and entertainment district in northwest Tel Aviv, Israel along the Mediterranean Sea.

spots.name: Azrieli Sarona Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Azrieli Sarona Tower is a skyscraper in the Sarona neighborhood, Tel Aviv, Israel, on Begin Road. It is 238.5 metres (782 ft) high with 61 floors. It is the third tallest building in Israel.

spots.name: Mahmoudiya Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mahmoudiya Mosque is the largest and most significant mosque in Jaffa, Tel Aviv, in the Tel Aviv District of Israel. It is composed of a complex of buildings arranged around two large courtyards and a third, smaller, courtyard.

names.ja: マフムーディーヤ・モスク

spots.name: Independence Hall

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Independence Hall, originally the Dizengoff House, is a history museum and the site of the signing of Israel's Declaration of Independence. It is located on the historic Rothschild Boulevard in Tel Aviv, Israel.

spots.name: Mikveh Israel
spots.summary: Mikveh Israel is a youth village and boarding school in the Tel Aviv District of central Israel, established in 1870.

spots.name: St. Peter's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Peter's Church is a Franciscan Catholic church in Old Jaffa, now part of Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel.

spots.name: Anu – Museum of the Jewish People

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Anu – Museum of the Jewish People, formerly the Nahum Goldmann Museum of the Jewish Diaspora, is located in Tel Aviv, Israel, at the center of the Tel Aviv University campus opposite Ramat Aviv. The Hebrew Anu אנו means 'we, us'.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Anu – Museum of the Jewish People

spots.name: Rabin Square
spots.summary: Rabin Square, formerly Kings of Israel Square, is a main large public city square in the center of Tel Aviv, Israel. Over the years it has been the site of numerous political rallies, parades, and other public events.

spots.name: Great Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Great Synagogue of Tel Aviv is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 110 Allenby Street, Tel Aviv, Israel. The synagogue is sited just east of the Shalom Meir Tower. It was designed by Yehuda Magidovitch and completed in 1926 in the Art Deco style.

spots.name: Ariel Sharon Park
spots.summary: Ariel Sharon Park is an Israeli environmental park. Situated along the lines of the Ayalon River in the area between Ben Gurion Airport and Highway 20, the area was intended to be the "green lung" of the southern part of the Gush Dan metropolitan area.

spots.name: Eretz Israel Museum

hours.note: Closed Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Eretz Israel Museum is a historical and archaeological museum in the Ramat Aviv neighborhood of Tel Aviv, Israel.

names.ja: エレツ・イスラエル博物館

spots.name: Beyond Towers
spots.summary: The Beyond Towers is a mixed-use skyscraper complex under construction in the Tel Aviv District city of Givatayim, Israel. Started in 2021, the complex consists of two main towers, an office building standing at 308.3 m (1,011 ft) tall with 72 floors, and a residential building with 50 floors.

spots.name: The Spiral Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Spiral Tower is a planned 91-story skyscraper, set to reach a height of approximately 350 metres (1,150 ft). It will be located at the Azrieli Center in Tel Aviv, Israel, and is slated to become the tallest building in the country.

spots.name: Tel Aviv Promenade
spots.summary: Tel Aviv Promenade runs along the Mediterranean seashore in Tel Aviv, Israel.

spots.name: Carmel Market

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Carmel Market is an outdoor marketplace in Tel Aviv, Israel.

spots.name: Habima Theatre
spots.summary: The Habima Theatre is the national theatre of Israel and one of the first Hebrew language theatres. It is located in Habima Square in the center of Tel Aviv.

spots.name: Kiryat Shaul Cemetery
spots.summary: Kiryat Shaul Cemetery is a 320-dunam Jewish burial ground in Northern Tel Aviv near the neighborhood of Kiryat Shaul. On the east side of the cemetery is a large military cemetery. Founded in 1943, it includes more than 80,000 graves, including those of Israeli political and cultural figures.

names.ja: キリャット・シャウル墓地

spots.name: Moshe Aviv Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Moshe Aviv Tower is a 235-metre-tall (771 ft) skyscraper located in the demarcated area of the Diamond Exchange District on Jabotinsky Road in the Tel Aviv District city of Ramat Gan, Israel. The 68-story building is commonly known as City Gate, its original name.

names.ja: モシェ・アヴィヴ・タワー

spots.name: Yarkon Park
spots.summary: Yarkon Park is a park in Tel Aviv, Israel, with about sixteen million visits annually. Named after the Yarkon River, which flows through it, the park includes extensive lawns, sports facilities, botanical gardens, an aviary, a water park, two outdoor concert venues and lakes. The park covers an area of 3.5 km².

spots.name: Saint Nicholas Monastery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Nicholas Monastery is an Armenian monastery built in the first millennium AD. Located in Old Jaffa, Tel Aviv, Israel, near the harbour and facing the Mediterranean, the monastery consists of a large multi-story complex that includes an Armenian church and living quarters.

spots.name: Dizengoff Street
spots.summary: Dizengoff Street is a major street in central Tel Aviv, named after Tel Aviv's first mayor, Meir Dizengoff.

spots.name: Sderot Yerushalayim
spots.summary: Jerusalem Boulevard, is a long historical avenue that crosses the city of Jaffa parallel to the shoreline a few hundred meters to the west, from the border of Tel Aviv to Bat Yam in the south to the Yehezkel Kaufmann Street in the north, where it continues as a boulevard to the beach.

spots.name: Kaplan Street
spots.summary: Kaplan Street is a major thoroughfare in central Tel Aviv, Israel, running from the Azrieli Center interchange on its eastern edge, to Ibn Gabirol Street on its western edge.

spots.name: Bauhaus Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Bauhaus Foundation, Tel Aviv is a private, non-profit museum and research center in Tel Aviv, Israel dedicated to the conservation, study and display of Bauhaus architecture, design, and art.

spots.name: Nahalat Binyamin
spots.summary: Nahalat Binyamin, also spelled Nachalat, Nachlat, and Nahlat Binyamin) is a street and neighbourhood in Tel Aviv, Israel that is partially a pedestrian zone.

spots.name: Railway Park
spots.summary: Railway Park is a linear public park in the neighborhood of Neve Tzedek in southern Tel Aviv, Israel. The park is on the route of the Ottoman railway between Nahalat Binyamin Street in the east and the station complex and Kaufman Street in the west. The park was partially opened to the public in October 2020.

spots.name: Immanuel Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Immanuel Church is a Protestant church in the American–German Colony neighbourhood of Tel Aviv Israel.

spots.name: Reading Power Station
spots.summary: Reading Power Station is a natural gas fueled thermal power station supplying electrical power to the Tel Aviv District in central Israel. It is in the northwestern part of the city at the mouth of the Yarkon River.

spots.name: Al-Bahr Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The al-Bahr Mosque, is the oldest extant mosque in the historical part of Jaffa, in greater Tel Aviv, in the Tel Aviv District of Israel.

spots.name: Ilana Goor Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ilana Goor Museum, or the Ilana Goor Residence and Museum, is an Israeli museum situated in the historical part of Jaffa, the Mediterranean port town south of Tel Aviv. The museum was founded in 1995 by Ilana Goor, an artist, designer and sculptor.

spots.name: Hassan Bek Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hassan Bek Mosque, also known as the Hasan Bey Mosque, is a mosque in Tel Aviv, in the Central district of Israel. The mosque was built between 1916 and 1923 at the northern boundary of Arab Jaffa; its history is closely tied to the Arab–Jewish conflict.

names.ja: ハッサン・ベク・モスク

spots.name: Bialik House

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Bialik House was the home of the Hebrew national poet Hayyim Nahman Bialik in the center of Tel Aviv, Israel, and is now used as a museum. The museum is located on 22 Bialik Street, Tel Aviv, close to the old city hall building.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.name: Ben-Gurion House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ben-Gurion House is a historic house museum in Tel Aviv, which served as the family home of pre-State Zionist leader and then first Defense and Prime Minister of Israel, David Ben-Gurion, between 1931 and 1953.

spots.name: HaYovel Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: HaYovel Tower also known as Kiryat HaMemshala Tower is a skyscraper in Tel Aviv, Israel. At 158 m, it is the 20th tallest building in Israel. Construction was completed in 2005 on land previously belonging to the IDF HaKirya base.

spots.name: Habima Square
spots.summary: Habima Square is a major public space in the center of Tel Aviv, Israel, which is home to a number of cultural institutions such as the Habima Theatre, the Culture Palace, and the Helena Rubinstein Pavilion for Contemporary Art.

spots.name: Fire and Water Fountain
spots.summary: Fire and Water, is a Tel Aviv art installation also referred to as the Dizengoff Square Fountain, is a landmark in the center of Dizengoff Square, Tel Aviv. Dedicated in 1986, the fountain is a kinetic sculpture by Israeli artist Yaacov Agam.

spots.name: Heichal HaTarbut
spots.summary: Heichal HaTarbut, officially known as the Charles Bronfman Auditorium and until 2013 as the Fredric R. Mann Auditorium, is the largest concert hall in Tel Aviv, Israel, and home to the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra.

names.ja: フレデリック・R・マン・オーディトリウム

spots.name: Ramat Gan Safari
spots.summary: The Zoological Center Tel Aviv-Ramat Gan in the Tel Aviv District city of Ramat Gan, Israel, is the largest collection of wildlife in human care in the Middle East. The 250-acre site consists of both a drive-through African safari area and a modern outdoor zoo.

spots.summary: The Israel Defense Forces History Museum is a museum dedicated to the history of Israel's military, from the underground organizations active during the British Mandate for Palestine to the modern Israel Defense Forces. The museum was built in southern Tel Aviv, next to the Jaffa Railway Station.

spots.summary: Reading Light, also known as Tell Qudadi Light, HaYarkon Light, Auja Light and Tel Aviv Light, is an inactive lighthouse in Tel Aviv, Israel.

spots.name: Begin Road
spots.summary: Begin Road is a major thoroughfare in Tel Aviv, Israel. It begins at Allenby Street and runs to its northern end which is at Arlozorov Interchange on Ayalon Highway.

spots.name: Lehi Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Lehi Museum, also known as Beit Yair is a museum in Israel about the history of the Lehi. The museum opened in 1985 and is operated by the Museum Department of the Ministry of Defense. It is located in the house where the founder of Lehi, Avraham Stern (Yair) was killed.

spots.name: Rothschild 22 Tower

spots.summary: Rothschild 22 Tower is a 29-story Israeli skyscraper reaching 117.9 meters in height, with an additional 9-meter tall decorative mast, and which covers an area of 1.9 dunam.

spots.name: Jaffa Light
spots.summary: Jaffa Light is a lighthouse in Jaffa, Tel Aviv, Israel. It is located on a hilltop above the old Jaffa Port, in the historical part of the city. It operated between 1865 and 1966, although now deactivated it is still used as a daylight navigation aid.

spots.name: Libyan Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Libyan synagogue of Jaffa is a Mizrahi Jewish synagogue built inside a former hotel in 1948 by Jewish immigrants from Libya. Located on Rehov Mazal Daggim, the Pisces (Fish) Street, in the historical part of Jaffa, it is the oldest synagogue in Tel Aviv-Yafo.

spots.name: Ramesses Gate
spots.summary: Archaeological remains from the 16th century BCE which can be freely viewed. However, they are hard to appreciate without a tour guide.

spots.name: Pagoda house
spots.summary: A large private house built in 1924. Designed with the guideline that it connect Eastern and Western architecture, its elements include Muslim arches, Greek columns, and of course a pagoda.

spots.name: Florentin neighborhood
spots.summary: A previously run-down but beautiful area, which is now gentrifying. Full of old, often colourful, Bauhaus buildings in various states of disrepair, however many of them are being renovated and restored to something approximating their former glory. The area is being completely redeveloped, and some construction of new apartment blocks is also taking place. This has caused some controversy with the

spots.name: Artist Workshops
spots.summary: For those with a passion for street art or an alternative hippie or punky side, this small quarter of artist workshops is covered with unusual, colourful, surrealistic, and political high-quality graffiti.

spots.name: Levinsky Market

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An extremely colorful outside market boasting a variety of spice shops and ethnic restaurants.

spots.name: Alma beach

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tel Aviv's only microbrewery and Israel's oldest continually operating microbrewery. Featuring 16 types of hand-crafted beers brewed on premises. Always an interesting seasonal beer or two (try the Golem - an Iced IPA at 11.3% on tap every full moon). Bar extends into the brewery so you can sit only a few feet from the copper brewhouse. Live Blues on Monday nights, Jazz on Tuesday nights. During F

spots.name: Molly Bloom's Irish Pub
spots.summary: The first Irish pub in Tel Aviv, great atmosphere and reasonable prices, busy at weekends. Has food and outdoor seating. Often many UK and Irish customers, strangely enough. Molly has another branch at 6 Aluf Albert Mendler St near HaShalom station. But no relation to Leo Bloom's Bar in the Ziv Tower out in the north city; fittingly so, since Molly's main problem with Leo was the "no relation".

spots.name: Mendalimos

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An Israeli pub and dance-bar. This is where a lot of the locals go to just to grab a beer or to enjoy the nightlife scene. Vintage design indoors, alongside outdoor balcony in which all the most important sports games are broadcast. Trendiest music from abroad and Israel.

spots.name: Salon Berlin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Laid back bar and trendy clothing store. When the hipsters tire of mingling at HaProzdor, they walk down here to sit down and chill with their friends. During daytime you may also check out the clothing store next door which boasts its own trendy clothing line.

spots.name: Mike's Place

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An American-style bar features live music every night of the week. Also features outdoor seating in the more pleasant weather, pool table and televised sporting events. Mostly Anglo 20-30 something crowd, very good bar with several kinds of beer on tap.

spots.name: Blackout

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: At this restaurant you eat a meal entirely in the dark, simulating the experience of blind people. Part of the Nalaga’at Center which works with blind and deaf people (see "Do" section above). Prior reservations are needed.

spots.name: Hummus Abu Dabi
spots.summary: Small laid back vegan hummus place. It's open onto the street so it's a great place to have lunch and watch the locals as they rush by while you relax to the sound of Reggae. Fridays tend to be especially crowded.

spots.name: 24 Rupi

spots.summary: Exemplifying the south Tel Aviv notion of chic, this is an Indian guest house-type restaurant/lounge established by Israelis enchanted by the India vibe, serving Tali and other Indian dishes.

spots.name: Tony Vespa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tasty and affordable Pizzeria. The Pizza is made in the style of Rome with a thick crust, many kinds of toppings, and is paid for according to weight. Great place for a late night snack.

spots.name: Hummus Eliyahu

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very delicious warm hummus with chickpeas, tahina and/or fava beans. Basic meal includes a refill, but it's not comparable to the Subway Coke refill you are used to in Europe.

spots.name: Ali Karavan Abu Hassan

spots.summary: Famous for its hummus, massabaha (coarsely textured hummus with whole chick peas), and ful (cooked spicy fava beans). Many Israelis claim it to be the best Hummus in Israel.

spots.name: Ozen Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Rock bar and venue. There are 2 shows nightly by the hottest local indie bands and even the occasional party. It's right above Haozen Hashlishit (The Third Ear) store.

spots.name: Dixie

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One of the first restaurants in Tel Aviv famous for being open 24/7, serves American food, including steaks, hamburgers and an excellent side-dish named home-fries.

spots.name: Abouelafia and Sons
spots.summary: The most famous bakery in Tel Aviv-Jaffa, if not in the entire country. Mounds of pastries and confectioneries. Israelis drive for miles to visit this bakery.
